skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count to 20 by 1s
skills.description: What number comes next when you count by 1s? Start at any number, like 7, 8, 9, and keep going to 20.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: What numbers are used for
skills.description: Numbers tell us how many, which one is first or second, and names like player number 24. Pick how the number is being used.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: See up to 5 at once
skills.description: Look quickly at some dots and tell how many there are, without counting one by one.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and type numbers to 20
skills.description: Match numbers from 0 to 20 to groups of things. Tap or type the number you see.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Counting up and counting down
skills.description: Count up and the number gets bigger. Count down and it gets smaller. Which way did it go?

skills.subject: math
skills.title: More, less, or the same
skills.description: Look at two groups and tell which has more, which has less, or if they are the same.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare numbers from 0 to 20
skills.description: Tell which of two numbers is greater or less. Find the number that is 1 or 2 more, or 1 or 2 less.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Estimate, then count to check
skills.description: Guess how many things there are. Is it closer to 5 or to 10? Then count to check.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Break apart and build 10
skills.description: Show that a number is made of two smaller parts, like 6 is 4 and 2. Find the missing part.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and take away to 5
skills.description: Put groups together or take some away when the numbers stay 5 or less. Know answers like 2 and 3 make 5.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract stories to 10
skills.description: Solve story problems about joining, taking away, parts, and comparing, with answers up to 10. Use counters or fingers to help.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Share equally
skills.description: Share things so every friend gets the same amount. Tell how many each friend gets.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Coins and bills
skills.description: Name Canadian coins and bills and tell what each is worth, up to 10 dollars. Loonies and toonies are coins too!

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and show numbers to 50
skills.description: Read numbers up to 50 in words and digits, and match them to tens and ones. Pick how a number is used, like on a clock or a house.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Skip count to 50
skills.description: Count to 50 by 1s, 2s, 5s, and 10s. What number comes next when you count by 5s? Use a number line or hundred chart to help.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare and order to 50
skills.description: Tell which number is greater or less. Put numbers up to 50 in order from least to greatest, or greatest to least.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Estimate up to 50, then count
skills.description: Guess how many things are in a group. Is it closer to 20 or to 50? Then count to check.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Build and break apart numbers
skills.description: Put numbers together or break them into parts, like 28 is 20 and 8, or 10 and 10 and 8. The amount stays the same.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fair shares for 2 or 4
skills.description: Look at the picture and tap what each friend gets when 2 or 4 friends share. Leftovers can be cut into equal pieces.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Halves and fourths
skills.description: Learn that one half of a whole is the same as two fourths of that same whole. Two halves or four fourths make one whole.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare shares of a whole
skills.description: When a whole is shared with more friends, each piece gets smaller. Look at the pictures and tap the biggest or smallest piece.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract facts to 10
skills.description: Know addition facts up to 10 and the take-away facts that go with them. For example, 4 and 6 make 10, so 10 take away 4 is 6.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Any order, zero, and checking
skills.description: Adding in any order gives the same answer, and adding or taking away zero changes nothing. Use adding to check a take-away answer.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Quick adding and subtracting to 20
skills.description: Use tricks like counting on, making 10, and near doubles to add and subtract in your head. Your answers stay 20 or less.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract stories to 50
skills.description: Use pictures, number lines, and equations to solve stories about joining, taking away, and comparing, up to 50. Find the missing number too.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Equal groups up to 10
skills.description: Look at the picture and tap how many in all, like 5 groups of 2, or 6 groups of one half. Or find how many groups there are.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and build numbers to 200
skills.description: Read and build numbers up to 200 with hundreds, tens, and ones. Break numbers apart in different ways, like 124 is 100 and 24, or 12 tens and 4 ones.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare and order to 200
skills.description: Tell which number is greater or less, up to 200. Put numbers in order from least to greatest or greatest to least.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Skip count to 200
skills.description: What number comes next when you count by 20s, 25s, or 50s? Start at any number and count up to 200, with coins or a number line to help.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Estimate up to 200, then count
skills.description: Guess how many are in a big group. Is it closer to 50, 100, or 200? Count a small bunch first to help, then count to check.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Even and odd numbers
skills.description: An even number can be split into pairs with none left over. An odd number always has one left over.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fair shares with leftover pieces
skills.description: Look at the picture and tap what each friend gets when up to 10 things are shared by 2, 3, 4, or 6 friends. Leftovers get cut into pieces, like 3 and one third.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: One third equals two sixths
skills.description: Share the same whole in thirds or in sixths. See that one third is the same amount as two sixths.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Adding and subtracting rules and checks
skills.description: Adding in any order gives the same answer, and zero changes nothing. Use adding to check taking away, and use equal jumps to see how adding links to multiplying.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract facts to 20
skills.description: Know adding facts with totals up to 20, like 9 + 9 = 18, and the take-away facts that go with them. Use doubles and making 10 to help.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Quick adding and subtracting to 50
skills.description: Add and subtract in your head with answers up to 50. Try counting on, making 10s, or taking away in parts.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract stories to 100
skills.description: Use objects, pictures, and equations to solve stories about joining, taking away, and comparing, up to 100. Find the missing number, wherever it hides.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Equal groups and repeated adding
skills.description: Find how many in all when there are equal groups, like 4 groups of 5. Groups of one half and one fourth count too.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Share up to 12 equally
skills.description: Share up to 12 things equally. Find how many in each group, or how many groups you can make.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and build numbers to 1000
skills.description: Read and build numbers up to 1000 with hundreds, tens, and ones. Match them to words, digits, and spots on a number line, like 638 is 600 + 30 + 8.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Place value of each digit
skills.description: Tell what each digit is worth in a number, like the 5 in 511 means 5 hundreds. See that a zero holds a place and that each place is ten times bigger than the one next to it.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare and order to 1000
skills.description: Tell which of two numbers is greater or less, up to 1000. Put numbers in order from least to greatest or greatest to least.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Round to 10 or 100
skills.description: Find the closest ten or hundred to a number, like 237 is about 240 or about 200. Use rounding to make a quick guess.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Skip count to 1000
skills.description: Count up to 1000 by 1s, 50s, 100s, and 200s. Start at any number and keep going, using a number line to help.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fair shares of up to 20
skills.description: Look at the picture and tap what each friend gets when up to 20 things are shared by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, or 10 friends. It can be a whole and a part, like 2 and two thirds.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Same share, different fractions
skills.description: See that different fractions can name the same amount, like one half and two fourths, or one fifth and two tenths. Use fair-share pictures to show it.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Show times and divide with arrays
skills.description: Use rows and columns of dots, called arrays, to show multiplying up to 10 × 10 and dividing up to 100 ÷ 10. Tell how many rows, how many in each row, and how many in all.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Facts for 2, 5, and 10
skills.description: Know the times facts for 2, 5, and 10, like 6 × 5 = 30. Know the matching share facts too, like 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Times and divide rules
skills.description: Use rules to help you multiply, like 4 × 5 is the same as 5 × 4, and 4 × 6 is 4 × 5 plus 4 × 1. Use multiplying to check a divide answer.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Times and divide stories
skills.description: Solve stories about equal groups using hops on a number line or pictures. Some groups can be one half, one fourth, or one third, and you can find the total, the groups, or the size of each group.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fractions as adding unit pieces
skills.description: See that three fifths is one fifth added three times. In a fraction like 3/5, the bottom number tells the size of the pieces and the top number counts them.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Scaling by 2, 5, and 10
skills.description: Use the pairs 1 to 2, 1 to 5, and 1 to 10 to make numbers bigger. If 1 smiley is 5 kids, then 3 smileys are 15 kids.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Quick adding and subtracting to 1000
skills.description: Add and subtract in your head with totals up to 1000, using tricks like making 10, adding in parts, or adjusting. Round first to make a quick guess.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Column adding and subtracting
skills.description: Add and subtract bigger numbers by lining up hundreds, tens, and ones. Trade ten ones for a ten, or a ten for ones, when you need to.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract stories to 1000
skills.description: Solve stories about joining, taking away, and comparing, with numbers up to 1000. Use number lines, pictures, or column adding, and find the missing number wherever it hides.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and build numbers to 10 000
skills.description: Read and build numbers up to 10 000 with thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones. Break them apart in different ways, like 8621 is 8000 + 600 + 20 + 1.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare and order to 10 000
skills.description: Tell which of two numbers is greater or less, up to 10 000. Put numbers in order from least to greatest or greatest to least.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Round to 10, 100, or 1000
skills.description: Find the closest ten, hundred, or thousand to a number, like 1237 is about 1200. If it is exactly in the middle, round up.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fractions from halves to tenths
skills.description: Look at the picture and tap the fraction it shows, like 3/4 or 7/10. Know what the bottom number and the top number mean.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare and order fair shares
skills.description: Look at the pictures and tap who gets more when a whole is shared by different numbers of friends. Put the shares in order from least to greatest.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Count and add unit fractions
skills.description: Count by halves, thirds, fourths, and more, even past one whole, like 5 thirds. See that 4 one-thirds added up is 4 × 1/3, or 4/3.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and compare decimal tenths
skills.description: Read, show, compare, and order numbers like 0.6 and 24.7. The first digit after the dot counts tenths.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Round decimals to whole numbers
skills.description: Round a number like 1.7 to the closest whole number. If it is exactly halfway, like 2.5, round up.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fractions and decimal tenths match
skills.description: Show that fractions and decimals can name the same amount, like 1/2 and 0.5, or 15 tenths and 1.5.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Rules and checks for operations
skills.description: Use rules like order, grouping, and splitting numbers to help you solve problems. Use opposite operations to check your answers.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Times and divide facts to 100
skills.description: Know all the times facts up to 10 × 10 and the divide facts that go with them, like 7 × 6 = 42 and 42 ÷ 6 = 7. Use facts you know to find new ones.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Multiply by 10, 100, and 1000
skills.description: In your head, multiply a number by 10, 100, or 1000, or divide it by 10. Each digit moves to a new place.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Quick adding and subtracting with tenths
skills.description: Add and subtract decimals like 14.9 + 24.6 in your head. Try making a friendly number, then fix it after.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract to 10 000
skills.description: Solve stories and problems by adding and subtracting numbers up to 10 000 and decimal tenths. Use number lines, pictures, or column adding.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Multiply by a one-digit number
skills.description: Multiply two- or three-digit numbers by a one-digit number, or by 10, 100, or 1000. Use arrays and split the number into parts to help.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Divide bigger numbers, share leftovers
skills.description: Divide two- or three-digit numbers by a one-digit number. When there is something left over, share it too, like 33 ÷ 4 = 8 and 1/4.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Rates: amounts per group
skills.description: Show rates like 2 trapezoids per hexagon or 5 stickers per strip. Use pictures and tools to find how many in all.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and build numbers to 100 000
skills.description: Read and build numbers up to 100 000 in words, digits, and expanded form. Break them apart by place value, like 24 336 is 2 ten thousands, 4 thousands, 3 hundreds, 3 tens, and 6 ones.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare and order to 100 000
skills.description: Tell which of two big numbers is greater or less by checking the biggest place that is different. Put numbers up to 100 000 in order from least to greatest or greatest to least.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Equal fractions, improper and mixed
skills.description: Show that different fractions can be the same amount, like 2/3 and 4/6. Switch between improper fractions and mixed numbers, like 7/4 and 1 and 3/4.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare and order fractions
skills.description: Tell which fraction is bigger, even when they are more than one whole. Use pictures, number lines, or the benchmark of one half to put fractions in order.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and compare hundredths
skills.description: Read, show, compare, and order decimals like 3.25. The second digit after the dot counts hundredths, and 3.2 is the same as 3.20.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Round decimals to the tenth
skills.description: Round a number like 56.23 to the closest tenth, which is 56.2. If it is exactly halfway, like 56.25, round up.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fractions, decimals, and percents
skills.description: Show that a fraction, a decimal, and a percent can name the same amount, like 1/4, 0.25, and 25%. Percent means out of 100.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Operation rules and checking answers
skills.description: Use rules like order, grouping, and splitting a number to make problems easier. Use opposite operations to check answers, even in problems with two steps.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Times and divide facts to 144
skills.description: Know all the times facts up to 12 × 12 and the divide facts that go with them. Know that zero times anything is zero.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Times 0.1 and 0.01, estimate decimals
skills.description: In your head, multiply a whole number by 0.1 or 0.01, like 400 × 0.1 = 40. Round decimals to make a quick guess for adding and subtracting.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add, subtract big numbers and decimals
skills.description: Solve problems by adding and subtracting whole numbers up to 100 000 and decimals to hundredths. Line up the places, and trade when you need to.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract same-size fractions
skills.description: Add and subtract fractions that have the same bottom number, like 3/8 + 2/8. You are just adding or taking away pieces of the same size.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Multiply two-digit by two-digit
skills.description: Multiply numbers like 24 × 38 using a rectangle split into four parts. Then do it with the written method.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Divide by a two-digit number
skills.description: Divide a three-digit number by a two-digit number, like 234 ÷ 18. Use a rectangle or the written method, and decide what to do with any leftover.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Multiply and divide by unit fractions
skills.description: Find 4 × 1/3 by adding four one-thirds. Find 4 ÷ 1/3 by asking how many thirds fit in 4 wholes.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Equal ratios and rates
skills.description: Make ratios and rates that mean the same thing by scaling up or down, like 6 green to 1 yellow is 12 green to 2 yellow. Use tables and pictures to help.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and build numbers to 1 000 000
skills.description: Read and build numbers up to one million in words, digits, and expanded form. Tell what each digit is worth, like the 5 in 527 910 is 500 000.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Positive and negative numbers
skills.description: Show numbers below zero, like -6, and numbers above zero, like 3, on a number line or with counters. Tell what -4 and 4 have in common.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Read and build decimals to thousandths
skills.description: Read and show decimals like 7.635 in words, digits, and expanded form. Compare and order them by looking at the biggest place that is different.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Compare integers, decimals, and fractions
skills.description: Put negative numbers, decimals, and fractions in order, even when they are mixed together. Use a number line and benchmarks like 0, one half, and 1.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Round decimals to tenth or hundredth
skills.description: Round decimals, even ones that go on forever like 3.555…, to the closest whole number, tenth, or hundredth. If it is exactly halfway, round up.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Fractions and decimals that match
skills.description: Change fractions into decimals and decimals into fractions, like 1/4 is 0.25 and 0.625 is 5/8. A fraction can also mean the top number divided by the bottom number.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Brackets and order of operations
skills.description: Use rules like order, grouping, and splitting numbers to make problems easier. Solve problems with more than one step, using brackets and the right order of operations.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Divisibility rules
skills.description: Use quick tricks to tell if a number can be shared evenly by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, or 10. For example, add up the digits to check for 3 or 9.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Percents of numbers in your head
skills.description: Find percents like 1%, 5%, 10%, 15%, 25%, and 50% of a number in your head. For example, 10% of 350 is 35, so 5% is half of that.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract with decimals
skills.description: Solve stories by adding and subtracting whole numbers and decimals. Guess the answer first by rounding, then find the exact answer and check that it makes sense.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Add and subtract different-size fractions
skills.description: Add and subtract fractions with different bottom numbers, like 1/2 + 3/4. Use fraction strips or a number line to make the pieces the same size.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Prime factors and factor trees
skills.description: Tell if a number is prime or composite. Break a number into prime factors with a factor tree, like 56 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 7.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Multiply by tenths
skills.description: Multiply a three-digit number by a decimal like 0.3, as in 235 × 0.3 = 70.5. Use an area model or multiply by 3 and then take one tenth.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Divide by tenths
skills.description: Divide a number by a decimal like 0.5. Make both numbers 10 times bigger so you can divide whole numbers, like 5 ÷ 0.5 = 50 ÷ 5 = 10.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Multiply a whole by a fraction
skills.description: Find 5 × 3/4 by thinking of 5 groups of three fourths. Use fraction strips or a number line, and give the answer as an improper fraction or mixed number.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Divide a whole by a fraction
skills.description: Find how many pieces like 3/4 fit into a whole number, such as 6 ÷ 3/4 = 8. Use pictures or rods to see the groups.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Divide decimals by whole numbers
skills.description: Divide decimals like 0.8 or 3.24 by a whole number up to 10, as in 0.24 ÷ 6 = 0.04. Use rods, grids, or short division.

skills.subject: math
skills.title: Ratios, rates, and percents
skills.description: Solve problems with ratios, rates, and percents by scaling up or down. Use ratio tables to find equal ratios, like 2 cups of sugar for 4 cups of fruit.
